The form factor of an alternating quantity is defined as the ratio of its Root Mean Square (RMS) value to its Average value.

$$\text{Form Factor} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{V_{\text{avg}}}$$

For a standard symmetrical sinusoidal waveform ($v(t) = V_m \sin(\omega t)$):
1. **RMS Value:** $V_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_m}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 V_m$
2. **Average Value:** $V_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2V_m}{\pi} ≈ 0.637 V_m$

$$\text{Form Factor} = \frac{0.707 V_m}{0.637 V_m} = 1.11$$

*(Note: Since the specific waveform image Fig. 3 is missing from the prompt text, the standard sinusoidal form factor derivation and value is given, which applies if the waveform is a pure sine wave.)*
